name: 'Silence' — Dae-jung Seo's Custom Katana
description:
A matte-black mono-edged katana. Carbon-nanotube composite blade end to end. Traditional silhouette, no electronics, no embedded systems, no charge state, no glow, no exotic discharge — by every measurable specification, a sword. What separates Silence from a museum piece is the molecular edge: a single row of aligned carbon nanotubes maintains a cutting surface that cannot be sharpened in any traditional sense. The edge does not dull. It chips. When it chips, the fractures propagate along the nanotube grain, and if left unrepaired, the blade eventually shatters. Kyle checks the edge every morning with three fingers along the flat, feeling for fractures. This is maintenance. This is prayer.

The blade has a reputation it does not deserve and never bothered to correct. On the street it shorts BCIs. It silences chrome. The hum of being augmented goes flat at the touch of it. Three different freelance blogs disagree on the mechanism — piezoelectric induction layer, neural-disruption coating, supercapacitor discharge — and a paid technical paper exists on each theory. None of them are correct. The blade is carbon nanotube and discipline, and the survivors who reported their augmentations going silent were experiencing the specific quiet that arrives in the half-second before a person realizes they are about to die. Augmentations going silent is not the same as augmentations being silenced. The brain edits the soundtrack. The blade just shows up.

Seo never corrected anyone. Kyle has not corrected anyone in a decade. The myth does more work than the blade ever could, and the myth costs nothing to maintain. The myth is the weapon. The katana is just the part that finishes the conversation.
manufacturer: Dae-jung Seo (custom fabrication — one of a kind, never reproduced)
tier_availability: One of a kind. Not available. Cannot be purchased, commissioned, or reproduced — Seo is dead and the construction process died with him. A handful of competitors have built credible-looking facsimiles for collectors; none of them have the molecular-edge nanotube alignment, which means none of them have the maintenance schedule, which means within a year of carrying one a fan is just carrying a heavy stick.
legality: Unlicensed — no registration was ever filed. The blade has no legal existence in any corponation database. Several enforcement systems have flagged it as a 'designated illicit melee weapon — class restricted,' which is the way corponation systems describe a sword whose owner they cannot find.
base_technologies: Carbon-nanotube composite blade — molecular-aligned edge construction, single-row nanotube cutting surface, monolithic blade body
Traditional kobuse-zukuri silhouette and proportions — built in the shape that works because the shape works
specifications: blade length: 71cm | total length: 102cm | blade width: 3.2cm at base | edge construction: aligned carbon-nanotube composite, single-row molecular edge | blade body: carbon-fiber matrix monolithic construction (no laminate, no shingane-kawagane distinction; the legend that it has a composite core is a misreading of the carbon-fiber visible grain) | tsuka: traditional silk ito over rayskin samegawa over the nakago, no electronic components | guard: tungsten carbide flat oval, unornamented | sheath: matte-black friction-fit composite, silent draw, superhydrophobic coating | weight: 0.94kg | edge service life: indefinite with maintenance; chips repair via specialist (none currently practicing in GLMZ — Kyle handles his own)
tactical_use:
It is a sword. The mode of operation is: get close, cut what needs cutting, leave. Kyle's style is rooted, positional, committed — Seo's training, the kata that select for the fighter who stands in rather than dances around. Cut accuracy matters more than speed; the molecular edge will pass through cyberware actuators, ballistic weave, and bone with the same effort if the angle is right and the line is committed.

What the blade is not good at: it will not solve a problem at range, it will not work through cover, it will not give Kyle a second chance against a target who has already drawn. Three meters of distance and a weapon that fires bullets beats Silence every time, which is the entire reason Chorus exists.
cultural_context:
A sword in 2225 is a statement before it is anything else. Carrying one means: I am close enough to touch you, and I chose to be here. In a city where the median freelancer fields a small armory of rifles and drone backup, the swordsman is making the claim that nothing else will be necessary. Kyle makes that claim with a straight face and walks home most nights.

The absurdity is structural. Every target Kyle has cut had roughly forty thousand credits of cyberware that did not save them. Every corponation security firm that has lost an asset to Silence has a postmortem report buried in legal that ends 'recommend countermeasure development' and gets reread once a year by a different intern. The blade is a contradiction in a city built on chrome: a piece of pre-electric craft that keeps winning against post-everything engineering. The street has spent decades inventing technical explanations for the contradiction because the alternative — that one well-trained man with a sharp metal stick can still resolve most freelance situations — is the kind of thing that breaks a corponation's research-and-development quarterly. So they say it shorts the BCI. They say the hamon glows. They say it stores kinetic charge. They say anything that lets them keep believing in the chrome.

Kyle has never once defended the blade in print. He prefers it this way. Laugh or you'd cry: the most dangerous weapon in West Town is a sword that has had three competing pseudo-engineering theories written about it, and the actual answer is the part nobody publishes.
known_users: Kyle Ellen Corbin (current wielder, inherited from Dae-jung Seo)
Dae-jung Seo (builder and original wielder, deceased)
story_hooks: A corponation R&D division finally green-lights a serious technical analysis of a Silence-class blade. They cannot find one to study. The intern assigned to acquisition meets Kyle in person and files a different report.

A copycat carries an obvious facsimile and starts cutting people for hire under the assumption Kyle's reputation will rub off. Kyle does not appreciate this. Sable is asked to clean it up before Kyle does.
naming_history: Seo never gave the blade a formal designation. During the years he carried it, he called it 'the blade.' The name Silence came from targets — the fragmentary accounts that circulated through GLMZ's freelance and criminal networks described the moment of contact as the most quiet they had ever experienced. No one ever asked Seo what the technical mechanism was, because the rumour was more compelling than the answer would have been. Seo acknowledged the name eventually. Kyle uses it because Seo used it, and Seo used it because his targets named it before he thought to.

physical_description.visual_profile: A katana that is mostly darkness. The blade is absolute matte black — light-absorbing rather than reflective. Carbon-fiber grain visible under direct light if you look for it. The temper line is just a faint difference in surface texture along the edge, not a colour, not a glow. Traditional silk ito wrap on the tsuka, kept dark. The whole weapon refuses to catch light, which is the entire point.
physical_description.dimensions: Blade length: 71cm | Total length with handle: 102cm | Blade width at base: 3.2cm | Guard diameter: ~6cm
physical_description.weight_description: 0.94kg. Balance point just forward of the guard. The carbon-fiber matrix is light for its strength; the blade feels nearly identical to a traditional katana of this length, with no dead weight in the tsuka because nothing electronic lives in there.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-nanotube composite blade (monolithic), tungsten carbide guard, traditional silk ito over rayskin tsuka, matte composite saya
physical_description.finish: Absolute matte black on the blade, no reflective surfaces anywhere on the weapon. The only break in colour is the white of the rayskin samegawa visible between the ito wrap diamonds — and that, half the time, Kyle keeps soot-darkened.
distinctive_features: Light-absorbing matte black blade — visible only as silhouette in most lighting
Carbon-fiber grain visible under bright direct light if you know to look
Traditional silhouette — every detail is the katana shape because the shape works
TSK-4 serial number laser-etched on the inner guard curve — relic of Seo's fabrication discipline; Kyle has never sanded it off
physical_description.condition_typical: The edge is meticulously maintained. Kyle checks for chip propagation daily. The rest of the weapon is unsentimentally kept.

visual_prompt: Product photography of a matte-black katana lying diagonally across a dark brushed-steel surface. The blade absorbs light. No glow, no luminescence, no electronics. Carbon-fiber grain barely visible under one focused light source. Traditional silk ito wrap on the handle, dark. A gloved hand grips the handle at the balance point. Neo-noir industrial aesthetic: cold rim lighting, rain-slicked concrete barely visible in background. Black on black, the only contrast is the difference between matte and gloss. 3:2 aspect ratio. --ar 3:2 --v 6
